skill.name: personwise-student-orientation
skill.description: Build grounded student orientation courses from institutional handbooks, policies, and supplied materials through the PersonWise digital-human course workflow.
skill.summary: Turn approved orientation materials into an interactive, source-grounded course that learners can question by voice.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, routine installer checks, and signed high-entropy data. The two vendor download URLs are confirmed low-severity network exposure. Semantic review found a high-risk remote update-command pathway plus medium risks involving disabled native signatures, external document uploads, and credit consumption.

remediation.issue: Update actions are accepted as command text from a service response.
remediation.suggestion: Parse structured update data and allow only fixed PersonWise subcommands with validated arguments. Reject shell strings, separators, substitutions, and unexpected executable paths.

remediation.issue: Native publisher verification is disabled for Windows and macOS releases.
remediation.suggestion: Require valid Authenticode and Apple signing identities before installation. Keep checksum verification as an additional integrity control.

remediation.issue: User documents are transferred to PersonWise for processing.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination, selected files, and data-handling notice before upload. Require explicit consent for every upload containing sensitive institutional or student data.

remediation.issue: A general creation request authorizes immediate consumption of existing credits.
remediation.suggestion: Show the credit cost and remaining balance before course creation. Require confirmation immediately before the credit-consuming command.

semantic_findings.title: Service Response Can Supply an Update Command
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to execute an action command returned by the CLI or service after approval, without defining a strict command-and-argument allowlist. A compromised response could turn the update path into arbitrary command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to run exactly the returned action command. They require approval but do not require structural validation before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Native Publisher Verification Is Disabled
semantic_findings.description: Windows and macOS bootstrap paths accept releases whose native signing status is deferred because signature enforcement is disabled. Pinned hashes provide integrity, but no independent platform publisher verification occurs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installers explicitly set native signature enforcement to false for affected platforms. Their signature checks therefore do not run for this release.

semantic_findings.title: Selected Documents Are Uploaded to an External Service
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uploads user-selected source documents to PersonWise for course processing. These materials may contain student, policy, or institutional data and leave the local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source add command takes an exact local path, and the surrounding text explicitly describes upload processing. Approval is required only for agent-discovered files.

semantic_findings.title: Course Creation Consumes Existing Credits Without Separate Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill treats a course-creation request as authorization to consume existing course credits. This can spend a limited account resource without a final transaction-specific confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The authorization rule explicitly says not to ask again before consuming a credit. It forbids purchasing credits, which limits the financial impact.

content.value_statement: Orientation materials are often scattered across handbooks, policies, and presentations. This skill turns approved sources into an interactive PersonWise course with review checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Designs a coherent student orientation arc from supplied institutional materials.
Creates and manages a durable course workflow through the PersonWise CLI.
Uploads explicitly selected documents and monitors their processing status.
Reviews outlines, scripts, images, and source support at defined checkpoints.
Publishes private or link-access courses when the user requests that access mode.
limitations: Requires the PersonWise CLI, browser OAuth, network access, and available course credits.
Uses only supported source facts for fees, visas, housing, accessibility, and safety policies.
Does not handle admissions decisions, academic teaching content, or individual student cases.
Cannot claim certification, learner competence, or real-world completion.

use_cases.title: Prepare New Student Orientation
use_cases.description: Turn current handbooks and welcome materials into a structured course before the next student intake.

use_cases.title: Orient International Students
use_cases.description: Build a source-grounded course that routes visa, fee, housing, and support questions to named offices.

use_cases.title: Standardize Orientation Delivery
use_cases.description: Create a reusable interactive course with reviewed scripts, consistent visuals, and clear support pathways.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Orientation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a private student orientation course from [handbook] and [welcome guide]. Use [page count] pages and cite the source year.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with named source files

prompt_templates.title: Focus on First-Week Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an orientation for [student group]. Cover accounts, registration, schedules, campus services, key policies, and support offices using only the supplied materials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused course for a defined cohort

prompt_templates.title: Build an International Orientation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private orientation for international students from [documents]. Route individual visa, fee, housing, and accessibility questions to the offices named in those sources.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Publish an Existing Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume course [project identifier]. Review every checkpoint for source support and consistency, correct objective issues, then publish with [private or link] access.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery, review, and publication workflow

output_examples.input: Create a five-page private orientation from the 2026 student handbook.
The handbook does not explain individual visa extensions. Add guidance.
output_examples.output: The supplied handbook does not support individual visa-extension guidance. The course directs learners to the international student office named in the source.

output_examples.input: Publish the reviewed orientation for anyone with the link.
output_examples.output: The course is published with link access after a fresh state check. The returned share link is provided as the public learner URL.

best_practices: Supply current, authoritative documents and identify the cohort or academic year.
Name the desired page count and access mode before course creation.
Review every checkpoint for factual support, progression, and consistent student guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented fees, visa rules, campus details, or staff identities.
Do not use this workflow for admissions decisions or individual student cases.
Do not upload unrelated local files or broaden course visibility without authorization.

faq.question: What source materials can I use?
faq.answer: Use current handbooks, orientation guides, policy documents, program materials, and approved campus images.

faq.question: Can the skill answer individual visa or fee questions?
faq.answer: No. It routes consequential individual questions to the office named in the supplied materials.

faq.question: Does it require a PersonWise account?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires browser OAuth, the compatible PersonWise CLI, network access, and available course credits.

faq.question: Can I keep the course private?
faq.answer: Yes. Private is the default when the user does not request broader access.

faq.question: Can learners ask questions during the course?
faq.answer: Yes. PersonWise courses support voice questions grounded in the approved course content.

faq.question: Does course creation prove learner completion?
faq.answer: No. The skill cannot claim certification, competence, attendance, or real-world completion.
